The boot has to keep water out and let the switch move. Get the wall thickness or the hardness wrong and you get a dead-feeling button on a perfectly good switch — we set both from the force you can allow.
It has to work in winter
Rubber stiffens as it cools, and a tailgate is opened outdoors with gloves on. We quote the actuation force at your minimum temperature, not at room temperature where every compound looks acceptable.
The wettest switch on the vehicle
A tailgate release sits low at the back, in the path of rain, road spray and the pressure washer. When the boot fails the switch fails — so we specify for ozone and UV, not just for the seal.

What is the minimum order quantity for this part?

We supply in bulk. The minimum run is 10,000 pieces per part number, per compound, or quoted against the part where geometry or tooling makes that unrealistic. Prototype and first-article lots sit outside the minimum.
Can you match a competitor specification or reverse-engineer an existing part?

Yes — and send the switch with the boot if you can. A boot removed from service has usually hardened, so copying its wall thickness reproduces a part that already feels stiff. We work back from the force the switch needs and the force you want the user to feel.
What file formats do you accept for drawings?

PDF, DWG, DXF and STEP. For this part a sample switch is worth more than a drawing. If you are sending files, mark the plunger travel, the panel aperture and the force the boot may add — and state the coldest working temperature.
Do you provide material test reports with each shipment?

Yes. Material test reports, dimensional inspection sheets and a certificate of conformance ship with every consignment. Hardness, tensile to ASTM D412 and compression set to ASTM D395 Method B are tested in-house, and actuation force is measured on batch samples.
What are your payment and delivery terms for international orders?

TT and LC accepted, discussed per order. Ex-works Nashik or FOB Nhava Sheva. Commercial invoice, packing list and certificate of origin are issued with every consignment. Boots ship bagged loose, not compressed.
